subtitle: One of the simplest steps in data prep -- and one of the easiest to get wrong.

steps.label: DISTANCE-BASED (kNN, k-means, SVM)
steps.sub: Big-value columns drown out small ones

steps.label: GRADIENT-BASED / REGULARIZED
steps.sub: Converges faster on a common scale

eyebrow: The wine dataset: wildly different ranges
code:
# alcohol:    11.0 - 14.8
# malic_acid:  0.7 - 5.8
# proline:   278.0 - 1680.0  <- varies by over 1,000!
caption: In a distance calculation, proline alone would decide almost everything.

eyebrow: Fit on training data only (same rule as Lesson 8)
code:
scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_tr)   # learn mean/std from TRAIN only
X_tr_s, X_te_s = scaler.transform(X_tr), scaler.transform(X_te)

# train column means: exactly 0 (by design)
# test column means: NOT 0 -- measured with the training yardstick
caption: Re-fitting a scaler on the test set would be peeking at it.

eyebrow: Scaling matters a LOT for kNN, not at all for trees
code:
knn: raw 0.722  ->  scaled 0.963
tree: raw 0.944  ->  scaled 0.944  (identical)
caption: Same test wines, same features -- scaling alone explains the kNN jump.
Real output: proline dwarfs everything raw; all four share a scale once standardized.

eyebrow: Choosing a scaler WITH an outlier (one value = 300)
code:
# standard: 5 ordinary values crushed to -0.47..-0.43 (outlier stretched the scale)
# minmax:   5 ordinary values crushed to 0.00..0.01
# robust:   5 ordinary values stay spread -1.0..0.6 -- outlier stays large, alone
caption: Default to standard. Use robust when outliers are present and you've chosen to keep them.

subtitle: Scale for distance/gradient/regularized models; skip it for trees.
